@@@ DivyamBanga__buildathon 6312225 11-21 00:15
Merge the on-demand imports and DuckDB reuse; state comparison for functions run at import; recalibrate
Expected practice score: ~150 s, anywhere from ~125 to ~190 (board-measured so
far: 189.5 s for e1fd283 = 170.3 s simulated + 19.2 s CPU; 765f19f not scored
yet).
Basis: the 240-commit benchmark generated like the organisers' sample costs
4.34 s simulated per commit at e1fd283 (the board: 4.26). Import-time changes
(765f19f) take about 0.9 s per commit off that; this commit turns three more
kinds of unchecked selection into checks (a default argument whose function
the executor tests call, a serde change, a harmless edit in a function that
sqlglot also runs while importing), at the price of more CPU. A back-to-back
measurement of the three commits on that benchmark is running; the next
commit message will carry its numbers.
Checked: 0 misses on the 30 sample commits, 216 mutants labeled with pytest
(labels from label runs that were paused long enough for a per-test timeout
to fire have been set aside and are being redone), 26 labeled benchmark
commits and 121 audit patches (100 of them with a failing test).

- From the other session's branch (reviewed): a patched module that the
  coordinator never imported is imported on demand in a hot child; DuckDB is
  kept closed until a test needs it and its recorded answers are reused after
  any class setup that sends the pinned statements; a test that reads a
  patched source file, or resolves the real location of its own file, gets
  the patched text.
- A function that sqlglot runs while it is imported (in some test's process)
  is covered by many tests that never call it themselves. Its candidates are
  now the tests that run it during the test, plus what the state comparison
  finds for what it did at import.
- Wider wall-clock and CPU allowances per test: under load test_max_nodes and
  test_qualify_columns were being stopped and counted as failing.
- Test costs measured again (gc thresholds as in the children; DuckDB answers
  after the tests' own setup).

of CPU on the board). Board anchor: e1fd283 scored 189.5 s = 170.3 s simulated

Two places where the previous three commits meet 765f19f:

- wants_probe required a clean job. A class or module body change in a module
  the coordinator never imported is now checked in a child that imports the
  patched module on demand (a hot job), and it must go through the comparison
  of import state all the same: that is what narrows its candidates, and what
  notices that the module no longer imports when tests were left out by the
  class narrowing. The mode is no longer part of the test; a plan with only
  function bodies to swap has no import-time candidates and is not compared.
- finish_probe replaces the candidates by rest_candidates plus what the
  comparison leaves. Tests that read a changed source as a file are now in
  rest_candidates as well, so the comparison cannot drop them.

@@@ DivyamBanga__buildathon bd5d384 11-20 22:48
Keep DuckDB closed until a test needs it; reuse its answers after any setup that matches
Expected practice score: ~188 s on top of 8f068a8 (~189 s). Board anchor:
e1fd283 scored 189.5 s = 170.3 s simulated + 19.2 s CPU over 40 commits.
Basis: 30 fixture-only commits cost 1.66 s CPU instead of 2.76 s (37 ms less

against the labeled mutant sets when this was committed.

- runner._ProbingConnection: in a child every plain duckdb.connect() returns
  a stand-in. While the statements it is sent are, one for one, those a
  pinned class setup sends (maps/ducksetup.json; paths compared with the
  checkout root marked, files the patch replaces excluded), DuckDB is not
  opened. After the whole setup, a query with a recorded answer
  (maps/duckdb.bin) gets it. Anything else opens the real connection, sends
  what was held back and is passed on; after a statement that is neither
  recognised nor a plain SELECT nothing is answered any more.

@@@ DivyamBanga__buildathon 765f19f 11-20 23:38
Compare what an import-time change leaves behind; close five ways to miss a failing test
Expected practice score: ~155 s, anywhere from ~125 to ~190 (board-measured
so far: 189.5 s for e1fd283 = 170.3 s simulated + 19.2 s CPU).
Basis: on 240 commits generated like the organisers' sample (one token changed,
files chosen uniformly), 7 changed code that runs at import and were selected
wholesale at 25-37 s each; they now cost 0-2 s. That is about 0.9 s per commit,
so ~37 s over the 40 practice commits if they resemble that set, and nothing if
the practice set happens to hold no such commit.
Checked: 0 misses on the 30 sample commits, 205 mutants labeled with pytest
(two further labels, m01144 and m01158, are timeouts of the labeling run on an
overloaded machine: one is a comment-only patch, the other passes under pytest
on a calm machine), 21 of 160 new import-time mutants labeled so far, 13
labeled benchmark commits and 116 adversarial patches from an audit.

New: selector/state.py. A module or class body runs once, at import, and can
only leave the package in another state. A child imports the whole package
pinned and patched and compares the two results object by object. No
difference: nothing to select. A function with another default or closure:
the tests that run it. A constant with a new value: the tests that read it.
Needs a second line map, tcov.bin (each test traced with sqlglot imported in
full first), so that what sqlglot runs while importing itself is not taken for
a test using it.

Fixes for ways a failing test could be left out (found by the audit):
- reads inside generator expressions and lambda defaults were attributed to the
  wrong code object and dropped from the reader map; each read is now looked up
  under the code objects that have instructions on its line;
- a class body that raises at import takes every importer of the module with
  it, not only the tests that reach the class: the comparison is always run
  when tests were left out that way, and widens the candidates again when a
  module no longer imports;
- an encoding declaration in a comment is honoured (files are compiled from
  bytes);
- Python outside sqlglot/ and tests/ that tests execute (sqlglotc/setup.py) is
  not verifiable in a child: its tests are selected as they are;
- a function that imports modules on demand runs when a module is first
  needed, which depends on the tests before: a change to one selects everything;
- a new test file that does more than define tests selects everything.

Also: memory allowance 2.4 GiB (test_max_nodes peaks 1.7 GiB above its parent
and was being stopped and selected whenever it was run), gc thresholds
(500000, 50, 1000) in children.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ DivyamBanga__buildathon e1fd283 11-20 21:22
Run one thing at a time: in-process pools, sequential children; complete case maps
Expected practice score: ~167 s (was ~173 s).
Basis: 30 sample commits on a quiet machine: 94.6 s simulated + 35.5 s CPU,
0 misses; practice = 1.175 x simulated + 1.586 x local CPU.
0 misses on 145 patches labeled with real pytest runs.

- The process pools the tests start are replaced by a stand-in that does the
  work in the test's own process, when its result is asked for (arguments and
  results are pickled as a pool would). No worker processes, and a failing
  test stops before the work it never looks at.
- Children run one at a time until the batch is 75 s in: two busy processes
  cost 10-15% more CPU for the same work.
- Per-case maps rebuilt from traces made with the fixed tracer (function
  first lines included); test costs measured again with the new runner.

@@@ DivyamBanga__buildathon 4a0265c 11-20 20:52
Recognise more changes that cannot alter behaviour; compare code by resolved instructions

Basis: 30 sample commits on a quiet machine: 100.8 s simulated + 33.9 s CPU,

- Code objects are compared as instructions with constants, names and jump
  targets resolved, so a constant table renumbered by the compiler (an edited

@@@ DivyamBanga__buildathon c7b8ac9 11-20 20:16
Fix coverage of one-line functions; cap CPU per test; probe before costly checks
- With line events alone, CPython 3.13 does not report a function's first
  line, so a one-line lambda was never seen running. The tracer now also
  monitors function starts, and the whole-test map is rebuilt from a trace
  made that way. Found by checking against patches labeled with real
  pytest runs.
- Case slicing no longer narrows when the per-case traces cannot account
  for a piece of changed code the test runs.
- A test that burns twice its normal CPU counts as failing.
- Before an expensive check, a few cheap tests are run to see whether the
  change is real.
- DuckDB's answers for the executor tests' queries are recorded once
  (keyed by the exact SQL text) and reused when that setup is untouched.

@@@ DivyamBanga__buildathon 15ed632 11-20 19:52
Slice fixture-driven tests by case, narrow constants to their readers, reuse executor tables
- maps/cases.*: for each fixture-driven test, the lines every single case
  reaches; only cases that reach the changed code (or that the patch edits)
  are run. The dialect loop of test_generator_memory is sliced the same way.
- A change to the value of a class or module constant is checked only
  against tests that execute a line reading it.
- Tests that share a class-level fixture load but do not depend on its
  cases are represented by one of them when only the fixture changed.
- The executor tests' TPC tables are parsed once and handed to children
  whose patch touches nothing that setup runs.
- A per-commit time budget, and the cost of checking measured per test
  (maps/runcost.json) and rescaled to the machine while running.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ DivyamBanga__buildathon bafdad2 11-20 19:36
Narrow class-level changes, weigh checking against selecting, validation tooling
- A change to a class body is checked only against tests that use the class
  (or its dialect) and, for a plain constant, that read it by name.
- Docstrings, string annotations and Python 3.13's per-class bookkeeping
  constants are not code changes.
- Tests are run cheapest first; once one fails, cheap remaining candidates
  are selected rather than run. The CPU cost of checking is measured as it runs.
- Runner: fixture-case filters, import check for files that only import a
  changed module, executor tables built once, DuckDB thread cap.
- tools/: labeling with real pytest runs, mutant generator, evaluation.

@@@ DivyamBanga__buildathon 2194200 11-20 18:52
Blast Radius selector: coverage map plus re-running affected tests

tests that executed a changed statement or opened a changed file. Those
tests are run against the patched code in forked children and only the
failing ones are selected, then split across workers.

@@@ Kalyan-Lankireddy__buildathon-sessions 2aa5f3d 11-20 21:50
v2.5 (experiment C): pread input into huge-page buffers, huge-page allocator with a reuse pool
Hypothesis: the scorer's extra time is page-fault cost on x86 (4 KB pages, many faults).
- Input is read with pread() in ~64 MB pieces, each into its own 2 MB-aligned buffer, and parsed
  right away while hot. No mmap of the input.
- A global allocator gives every allocation of 2 MB or more a 2 MB-aligned block with
  madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE). Allocations under 2 MB are untouched (the 256 per-chunk shard buffers
  are about 220 KB each, so they still use 4 KB pages).
- Freed big blocks are kept in a pool (cap 3 GB, fixed arrays, no allocation inside the allocator)
  and reused by later big allocations of similar size, so later stages skip page faults and zeroing.
- Dockerfile: back to -C target-cpu=x86-64-v3 (cascadelake build B is a separate commit, 83f1afd);
  explicit --target kept.

Gates passed (this exact code): 36/36 fixtures and make check-dev MATCH through the amd64 image;
20M seed 7 exact vs the DuckDB reference both native and through the image; stage-by-stage exact
on seeds 2, 3, 4 (1M) and 5 (5M); timestamp cross-check vs reference ts_ms; unit tests for
read_map (7 chunk sizes, empty/header-only/no-trailing-newline files) and the allocator.

Not benchmarked locally (the Mac cannot show THP effects); the scorer is the judge.
Memory: 20M peak 5.1 GB anon (v2.2: 4.46 GB incl. 1.8 GB mapped input). Expect about 15 GB at 60M.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ Kalyan-Lankireddy__buildathon-sessions 83f1afd 11-20 21:35
v2.4 (experiment B): build with -C target-cpu=cascadelake (AVX-512), explicit --target
- RUSTFLAGS now cascadelake; cargo uses an explicit --target so the flag applies only to our
  binary, not to build scripts (they run on the builder and must not need AVX-512).
- The arm64 timing loop builds with --build-arg RUSTFLAGS="" CARGO_TARGET=aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.

Gates: identical source to v2.3 (16f0c6f), which passed all gates, built with x86-64-v3. The
cascadelake binary cannot run locally (Rosetta has no AVX-512; the local run hangs), so it has NOT
been gated locally. The image builds cleanly for linux/amd64. The scorer's exactness check is the
gate for this build; if it rejects or is not faster, go back to v2.3.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ Kalyan-Lankireddy__buildathon-sessions 16f0c6f 11-20 21:16
v2.3 (experiment A): thread pool size from NCPU only (default 8); bucketed sort, F2 day cache
- rayon pool = NCPU env var, falling back to 8, never the detected CPU count.
- Person sort: one bucketing pass on the top person bits, then per-bucket sorts in cache.
- Intern computes its own per-source counts (one fewer pass over the records).
- Day cache also covers the F2 (offset) timestamp form; randomized test vs the strict parser.

Gates passed (this exact code): 36/36 fixtures and make check-dev MATCH through the amd64 image;
20M seed 7 exact vs the DuckDB reference through the image; stage-by-stage exact on seeds 2, 3, 4
(1M) and 5 (5M); timestamp cross-check vs reference ts_ms on 600k strings.
Local 20M (linux/arm64 VM, 8 cpus, min of 7): about 1.31 s, cpu 6.7 s (v2.2: 1.43 s, 7.1 s).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ Kalyan-Lankireddy__buildathon-sessions c939079 11-20 20:54
v2.2: inline keys, in-place dedup, fast F1 timestamps, flat product table (about 40% less CPU)
- Event/click/user IDs are stored inline as 16-byte keys in the parse records (exact: keys over
  15 bytes keep a pointer and compare bytes). No pointer chasing in dedup or intern.
- Dedup marks losing copies dead in place (no gather copy, no survivor copy); flatten only clicks.
- Intern reads keys straight from the records (no keys/hashes arrays), two-phase shard tables.
- Timestamps: day-prefix cache for the F1 form, single-pass digits for F3 (strict parser is the
  fallback and the reference for tests).
- Flat open-addressing product table over inline keys instead of HashMap.
- Dropped malloc_trim (it did not lower the peak and cost CPU).

Gates passed (this exact code):
- 36/36 fixtures through the amd64 image; make check-dev MATCH through the image
- Rust == DuckDB reference (exact, stage by stage) on seeds 2, 3, 4 at 1M, seed 5 at 5M;
  seed 7 at 20M exact both native and through the image
- timestamp cache and parser vs the reference ts_ms on 900k strings; unit and randomized tests
- rules.md self-checks

Local timings, 20M (seed 7), linux/arm64 in Docker VM, 8 cpus, min of 7, noisy shared machine:
1.43 s total, cpu user 6.5 s + sys 0.9 s (was 2.33 s, user 10.0 + sys 2.5 at v2.1).
Peak memory 20M: 4.46 GB total incl. 1.8 GB mapped input (v2.1: 4.29 GB).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ Kalyan-Lankireddy__buildathon-sessions 0fee302 11-20 19:17
v2.1: lower memory, hash-table dedup, carried hashes, word-at-a-time field splitter
- Records route into 256 hash shards while parsing (no partition copy); Ev 48/56 B, Ck 56 B,
  survivors 32 B. malloc_trim after big frees, eager drops. 60M peak anon about 6 GB (was 9+).
- Dedup by exact open-addressing table (was sort): 0.78 s -> 0.28 s on 20M.
- user_id pointer and 32-bit hash taken at parse time; intern scatters values and prefetches.
- Field splitter finds commas and quotes eight bytes at a time (tested against a plain splitter).
- Stage timers, RSS and CPU time on stderr; scripts/linux_run.sh and bench_linux.py.

Gates passed:
- 36/36 fixtures through the amd64 image; make check-dev MATCH through the image
- Rust == DuckDB reference (exact) on seeds 2, 3, 4 at 1M, seed 5 at 5M (stage by stage), seed 7 at 20M
- rules.md self-checks

@@@ Kalyan-Lankireddy__buildathon-sessions 2aea8b8 11-20 17:41
v1: check-dev pass, 36/36 fixtures, local 1M run 6.9 s in amd64 image
Correctness baseline on DuckDB. Raw line reader (read_text, split on LF) because
DuckDB read_csv treats a bare CR as a line end. Links via scipy connected
components, credit via ASOF join, assists via range join.

Checked through the linux/amd64 image with scorer flags: make check-dev MATCH
(117038 user_daily rows, 27400 campaign_daily rows), 36/36 fixtures, 167 unit
tests. Base image, duckdb, numpy and scipy are pinned. DuckDB uses 8 threads,
a 20 GB limit and /scratch for temp files.

@@@ Kgc3105__MAGIC-Royale aace465 11-21 10:30

On 600 fresh simulated matches this scored 5.96 against 5.71 for the
previous settings (+0.25 +/- 0.07). A milder version of the same bundle
gave +0.23 and +0.19 on two separate sets.

  out-gunned by a laser; leave hiding at 50% health. A house bot only
  dies if we kill it, and every step toward fighting on has paid off.

@@@ Kgc3105__MAGIC-Royale f0a85ee 11-21 06:34
Kite at long range with the laser; stop runtime threads stalling answers
- With a laser, hold 125-185 m and back away firmly (boosting if a mech
  gets well inside that): at that range gun fire can be dodged while the
  beam still lands. Retreat picks a reachable spot away from every mech.
- Dockerfile: compile on the main thread, skip the slowest compiler
  tier and use one GC marker. Under the 1-CPU limit the runtime's extra
  threads could use up the allowance and freeze the bot past the 50 ms
  budget (worst answer 55-114 ms in the sandboxed check); now about 16 ms.
- Rehearse a few hundred made-up decisions at start-up so compilation
  happens before the match.
- Numeric overrides and switches for local experiments (MECH_TUNE,
  MECH_DROP, MECH_SLOW_MS); supply drops under fire tested neutral, off.
- Simulator: damage-source, kill-timing and laser statistics.

@@@ MauroMiranda28__mech-royale-bot 47a1d91 11-21 02:14
v20: duel micro - dodge their lead, fight at 100 m, heal between fights
Diagnosis: v14 lost 1v1 duels to the simple sim hunter 40:99 (gun) and
29:111 (lightning): equal fire rate, but they hit us 83% vs our 79%.
- STRAFE 0.25-0.5 s, always reverse, sideways weight 1.6: reversing
  faster than a bullet's 0.3-0.5 s flight beats a velocity lead
- FIGHT_BOOST_E 70: boost less in fights (slower reversals otherwise)
- GUN_FIGHT_RANGE 75 -> 100 m: longer flights, more misses on us
- LIGHTNING_BRAWL off: rushing to 28 m lost duels (84:60 vs 100:40)
- REGEN_FIRST 0.9: don't shoot crates / drones below 90% HP (dealing
  damage blocks regen)
- Duels vs hunter (gun): 116:21 (was 40:99); vs smart: 127:13
- Full-match arena (300): v20 8.90 vs v14 7.70, survives 111 s vs 78 s

Root causes of ghost-v1's 2.48 (details in experiments/ROOT_CAUSE_ANALYSIS.md):
- crates never read; drones fought only after they hit us; loot radii 26/38 m
- combat only reactive (provoked / <50 m / weak); flat 35% retreat; no recovery state
- combat had no zone term; gunfire sounds ignored; supply drops only within 110 m

Changes (every behaviour is a flag/number in ghost_bot.CFG):
- _farm: crates, drones, cubes, laser/lightning pickups while calm and above 55% HP
- _choose_fight/_pref_range/_duel: kill-time based fight selection, range by loadout,
  retreat 28% + 7% per extra enemy, recover vs flee, zone push near the rim
- supply-drop reach 260 m, sound pre-aim, new upgrade order
- ghost-v1 kept frozen in baseline/ghost_bot_v1.py (byte-identical to e3fbf79 ghost_bot.py)
- tests/test_v2.py (32 decision tests), tests/arena_sim.py (squad-hunt simulator),
  experiments/ (root-cause analysis, ledger, v1 vs v2 simulator results)

Validation: official check/check.py PASS plain, 1 CPU and uid 65534 (300/300 in time,
p99 <= 7.5 ms, max 9.2 ms); simulator v1 3.17 -> v2 3.57 mean over 4 conditions (inside noise).
Docker build not run (no Docker daemon in the workspace).

@@@ arnabxero__xero-mech-royale 84f1112 11-20 21:57
v5.2: latency-compensated gun lead
Shots leave 1-2 ticks after the observed state: solve the gun intercept from the target advanced
by 0.05 s and from our own muzzle advanced by our velocity; the laser release aim also accounts
for our own motion (gun_lat=0.05, self_comp on). Adds optional knobs gun_tol_m, gun_tol_rad,
laser_tol_m, gun_far, pref_gun, pref_laser (defaults unchanged).

@@@ arnabxero__xero-mech-royale 127088b 11-20 21:45
v5.1: hold the trigger when a cooldown ends inside the decision window
The server fires as soon as a weapon's cooldown ends while the trigger is held. We used to pull
the trigger only when the cooldown was already 0 at decision time; with 0.1 s decisions the
0.24 s gun effectively fired every ~0.3 s (about 20% less DPS). Same for laser charge start,
lightning and mortar. Switch: fire_early (on).

@@@ arnabxero__xero-mech-royale 50ea7de 11-20 21:32
v5.0.1: optional knobs (tactical reload, heal in cover, shoot_close); simulator models
Default behaviour is unchanged from v5. New XERO_TUNE switches:
- tac_reload: reload while the target is out of line of sight and the magazine is half empty
- cover_heal_hp: stay in cover until this HP fraction (up to 30 s) unless an enemy is within 45 m
- shoot_close: open fire on enemies closer than this even when not engaged (default 50 m, as v5)
Simulator: squad3 practice model (infighting knob), non-leading opponents (SQUAD_NOLEAD),
rear-damage and raw accuracy stats, server benchmark scripts.

@@@ bsrikumar855-dot__Mech-Royale fe8bb4b 11-21 10:53
feat(locomotion): tactical utility scorer with 3D cover, mortar dodge, FOV threat, and rim timing
Single-variable experiment: ONLY locomotion changes. Combat, Economy, Arbiter and Session are
byte-identical to 3fae0bf (score 1.90, BB-C7F0AB94).

Candidates (~33-45 per tick): hold, goal steps toward the zone (with +-65/+-105 deg wall-tangent
slides when the direct line is blocked), a loot step, and rings at 4.5/11/24 m. Every candidate is
reachable in a straight walk on MapQuery (step-up, slope, prisms, low decks, map edge, cube-scaled
body) or clamped to its last walkable point.

Utility terms: zone (cliff outside, urgency-scaled pull to the next circle, rim plateau with a mild
dead-centre penalty while > 5 alive), 3D cover against the top-6 tracked enemies (fov wedge /
near-range, charging-laser x4, laser x1.4, lightning x1.8, distance falloff, super-linear crossfire,
HP scaling, regen discipline), path-midpoint exposure, mortar impact prediction (parabola vs terrain
and buildings), bullet corridors, spacing (mechs, drones when hurt), caution toward unseen fire,
safe loot, silent-hold bonus, move cost, hysteresis (off during laser/mortar emergencies),
wall-slide side commitment, and an anti-stuck tangent bias. Boost is a latched controller
(emergency down to 8 energy; tactical start 35 / hold 18). jump stays false.

Warm-up before ready: 2 -> 300 synthetic decisions so V8 optimises the scorer before the match
(one-core p95 4.8 -> ~1.6 ms). WorldModel gains a read-only resetCount so locomotion memory resets
with the world.

Tests: 153 pass (locomotion suite rewritten, 47 tests); 16 of 16 deliberate rule breakages caught.
Worst case (15 enemies, 80 cubes, 40 pickups, 10 projectiles, real map) p99 ~1.0 ms.
Known regression: on the one-core pinned proxy, tick p99 rose from ~3.5 to ~15-21 ms (rare
JIT/deopt pauses in paths the synthetic warm-up does not cover); 0% late; unpinned p99 1.7 ms.

@@@ bsrikumar855-dot__Mech-Royale 3fae0bf 11-21 10:13
feat: Phase 1 MVP rules (economy, combat, locomotion), simple rules only
Economy: all 22 upgrades ranked (survival/mobility first) and picked on every offer; take ONLY
lightning into an empty slot within reach (mortar/laser skipped on purpose); LootTargets for cubes
and wanted lightning pickups, value falling with distance.

Combat: nearest/weakest visible enemy mech with clear shot LOS; drones only within 35 m and only
when no mech is visible; linear gun lead from the real muzzle with the upgraded projectile speed;
fire gate on the ACTUAL slewed aim (0.15 rad) with ammo/reload checks; lightning in cone/range/
energy; proactive reload; defensive facing via threatBearing (damage > unshootable enemy > last
seen > combat sound).

Locomotion: zone safety against zoneAt(t+10) with boost only when outside the zone; kiting that
stays inside the safe zone; short safe loot detour; stand still otherwise; wall feeler that steers
+-30/60/90/120 deg using MapQuery. No utility grid, no hysteresis, no pathfinder.

131 unit tests (up from 60), including closed-form lead intercept, the 90-degree slew gate, steering
around a real arena wall, and a worst-case perf test. Mutation-checked: 9 of 9 deliberate breakages
of the key rules fail a test. Node 22.23.5 check.py PASS 300/300; pinned-core p99 3.5 ms.

Docker build and sandboxed check.py are still unverified (no Docker on the dev machine).

@@@ bzells11__Mech-Bot-Repo- b1b77da 11-20 23:13
Mech Royale variant L: fight read decides run or stay, laser kit
Run or stay now comes from the awareness picture instead of an HP line:
the fight is played forward with everyone who has a line on us plus
enemies that know where we are and are close enough to join, killed
quickest first. Lose that, or win with under 15% to spare, and it runs;
hit by someone unseen, it runs. Adds the tracker (where every enemy it
has seen or heard is now) and the reasoner (one intent and one target,
trigger discipline). Kit: laser + gun.

Local sim, 48 practice matches (seeds 11, 23): 0.77, up from 0.29 for
the same brain with the HP rule. check.py passes in the 1-CPU docker
sandbox (max answer 16.6 ms).

@@@ charliescull__mech-royale-bot 2495a99 11-21 00:19
Mech Royale variant M6: veteran brain, F-style practice mode
Practice (house squad) plays like F: never leaves a fight, shoots on
sight; cover, heal and reposition are off there because they cost
points against a vision-sharing squad (1.61 vs 1.30 over 96 sim
matches). Free-for-all keeps the veteran tactics: fight from the side
of cover with peeks and a laser jump-shot, reset to heal, move after a
kill. Also: keep every threat in front (flanked deaths 38% -> 6%),
tree-aware sight, HP-first veteran kit.

@@@ colton-boi__Mech-Bot b2e8df5 11-20 19:42
fix(bot): keep returning fire and stay in retreat until healed
Below 40% HP the retreat state went silent even while still being shot,
which bought nothing since incoming damage already resets the regen clock.
It also dropped out after the 6 s threat window, one second into regen,
and re-engaged. Now it fires back while hits land, holds fire once they
stop for 2 s, and stays in retreat for up to 20 s until HP is back to
resume_frac.

Also count a failed roof climb once per attempt instead of every airborne
tick, and quantize the aggro chase goal to 20 m so its flow field can
finish instead of restarting every tick.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ colton-boi__Mech-Bot deb231a 11-20 19:38
test: add injected-scenario harness and kinematic walk check
check.py replays 30 s of non-reactive observations and mf.run swallows
exceptions, so it cannot show that rare states work. The harness calls
Bot.act directly on the stream with injected enemies, shells, damage,
offers, drops, low HP and out-of-zone, validates every action, and times
it. `harness.py walk` feeds the bot its own moves against the wall raster
to check it reaches the zone. tools/ is kept out of the image.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ colton-boi__Mech-Bot a8e0d13 11-20 19:38
feat(bot): add survival state machine with four strategies
Score is placement by death order, so the default strategy optimizes for
staying alive: move to the next zone circle early, hold still beside a
building, face the last attacker (rear hits deal 1.5x), back off and hold
fire to regen when hurt, dodge mortar shells and aimed lasers, lead gun
shots, take better weapons and supply drops only when no enemy is around.

Each strategy is data in PARAMS: an ordered list of states (first whose
predicate holds wins) plus a fire policy. strategy.txt next to bot.py picks
one of survive (default), hide, roof and aggro, so probe variants are a
one-line change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ colton-boi__Mech-Bot 92be1ae 11-20 19:38
feat(bot): add map model with line of sight and flow-field navigation
The bot needs the static map to avoid walking into walls while the zone
closes, to know when a shot or a sight line is blocked, and to find cover
and climbable roofs. world.py loads terrain.i16 and rasterizes every prism
(holes included) at 2 m, derives a 4 m walkability grid (walls plus slopes
over max_slope_deg), cover distances, walkable components, a time-sliced
BFS flow field so path search never blows the 50 ms budget, and roof
candidates with ground approach points. Loads in about 0.7 s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ dmclaughlin-bit__mech-bot 69cdae0 11-21 05:25
Build 16: kill-value target selection
Replace nearest-clear targeting with a kill-value pick and a lock (target.ts).
Each enemy mech in view is scored on: a shot from here (clear line and a
weapon in range), time-to-kill from our weapon stats, low hp/max_hp, weak
weapons, and being alone (no other enemy within 40 m). The best one is locked
until it dies or has had no shot for 3 s. While the lock is briefly lost, any
other shootable enemy is shot without moving the lock. An enemy outside the
circle is picked only while we can shoot it from where we stand. Movement is
unchanged.

TARGET_PICK_ON in params.ts rolls back to Build 13 exactly (same actions as
origin/main on the kit recording, with and without a synthetic second enemy).
tools/target_check.ts counts targets, switches and picks offline.

@@@ dmclaughlin-bit__mech-bot 7c14e83 11-21 05:00
Build 14: fight-or-flee (TTK vs TTD)
Replace "retreat on our HP alone" with a time-to-kill vs time-to-die test.
Weapon DPS and reach are read from hello.config.weapons at hello.
ttk = enemy hp / (our in-reach weapon DPS x hit-rate guess x cube bonus);
ttd = our hp / (sum of DPS of enemies with line of sight to us, by their
observed weapons). When the HP retreat would trigger and exactly one enemy
threatens us, fight on while ttk < params.aggression x ttd. Also commit to a
target at or below one magazine of our weapon while no second enemy sees or
hits us, then walk to its cubes if safe. Otherwise the existing retreat runs
unchanged, and zone safety ranks first. ENGAGE_ON in params.ts rolls back to
Build 12 behavior. Adds tools/engage_check.ts (offline counts on recorded
observations, not scores).

@@@ georgegcal1-arch__mech-royale-bot 841db86 11-21 00:20
v4: survive longer
- Below 50% HP break off: head for a spot (no closer to any visible enemy,
  inside the zone with margin, reachable in a straight line) where a
  building or the ground hides us from every visible enemy, stand still
  there, hold fire unless an enemy is within 20 m, resume at 90% HP.
  Torso keeps facing the threat.
- Quiet: with no enemy mech in view, move below the footstep speed unless
  the zone forces a hurry.

- Zone first: zone hurry overrides retreat; cover and NPC detours stay
  inside the zone; outside it nothing deflects the run back.
- Safety net: fallback answers an upgrade offer; non-finite numbers in the
  action or debug drawing no longer produce invalid JSON.
- world.py: prism grid + clipping to the map (line cost bounded by map
  size, not line length), solid_at() for cover spots.

@@@ gonvaz-nocode__NoCodeHack cbc06b1 11-20 17:39
Fix zone-trap oscillation in coarse navigation; add tools
geo.steer: when the mech stands in a coarse cell whose centre sample is
blocked, head for the neighbouring cell that is best toward the goal and
walkable from here, instead of the nearest free cell centre. The old rule
could point away from the goal and make the mech shuttle across a cell
edge forever (practice seed 1: stuck at (57, 223) from 110 s, died to the
zone at 201 s, 0 points).

bot: stuck detection also checks net progress while travelling outside
combat (< 4 m in 4 s triggers the unstick move), since a mech shuttling at
full speed never looked stuck to the speed-only check.

Also adds three behaviour switches, all OFF by default and unchanged
behaviour unless SURVIVOR_FLAGS is set: pick (fight only threatening
mechs), cover (exposure-weighted routing using tall buildings and tree
canopy), creep (walk below the footstep threshold near enemies). Sim A/B
over 120 practice + 15 ffa seeds: pick -0.9 pts/match, cover and creep
within noise.

tools/record.py: record sim matches as replays for the viewer.
tools/debug_stuck.py, tools/debug_coarse.py: diagnose navigation loops.
tools/bench_rollout.py: line-of-sight, rollout and memory benchmarks.

Checked: kit check.py PASS (300/300 in time, max 10.1 ms), peak memory
155 MB.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ koillea__mech-royale-goonies 7a4f118 11-21 05:09
try-peek: v3.5 + corner fighting (one change)
In a fight the planner chose (a mech that hit us or is inside 90 m), on the ground, 20-200 m away: if a
corner is within 10 m (a spot hidden from the target even 1 m off it, with a peek spot 2.5-5.5 m away that
sees the target), alternate PEEK (stand at the peek spot, fire for 1 s, or until the gun is dry or the laser
has fired) and DUCK (back into cover for 0.6 s, reloading when below half). No corner: strafe as before.
No long runs to cover and no hiding until healed (v4's likely mistakes). Corner search capped at 6 ms.
Seen on the cast: strong bots peek from cover with burst fire and never fully commit.

@@@ koillea__mech-royale-goonies cf8d2a4 11-21 02:57
C: intel tracking, cover when shot, fire back from the best angle
- intel.py: per-enemy estimates from sight, beams (exact shooter position), damage bearings (distance from a
  matching gunfire sound), incoming bullets, and sounds (footsteps, boost, jets, reloads, weapons);
  confidence decays (half-life 3 s); anonymous estimates merge by bearing and fold into seen mechs.
- Cover when shot (not before every fight, unlike v4): nearest spot hidden from the shooter and, per intel,
  from other mechs, preferring a firing spot toward the shooter on its back side and higher; hide (reload,
  regen, pre-aim), peek, duck back.
- Fixes for v4's likely failure modes: fight back against pushers (< 25 m) and flankers who see us in cover
  (< 70 m), stand and fight after 3 relocations in 6 s, zone always first.
- Pre-aim at heard threats; spot choice avoids places intel says are occupied.
- tests/test_intel.py, tests/test_combat.py.

@@@ koillea__mech-royale-goonies e8feab6 11-21 02:52
B: refined aim - motion prediction, pre-aim, rear-arc preference
- aim.py TargetTracker: 2 s history per target; steady movers use current velocity, strafers (2+ reversals
  across our line of sight) the window's drift velocity; airborne targets fall with gravity, never below
  ground; predictions never pass through walls. intercept() solves flight time against that prediction.
- Gun, laser and mortar aim through the tracker (decision latency included).
- Pre-aim: with no target, the torso tracks the nearest visible mech half a second ahead, or where a mech
  that hit us was heading after it hid (up to 2 s), instead of sweeping.
- Rear armour (x1.5, the game's only positional damage bonus): prefer targets facing away; 70 % of strafe
  legs walk around toward the target's back.
- tests/test_aim.py (10 cases).

@@@ koillea__mech-royale-goonies 9cd3063 11-21 02:35
v4: cover-first combat, laser hunting, decision-time hardening
- model._combat: against a mech never trade shots in the open. COVER (exposed or just shot: run to the
  nearest spot the threat cannot see, inside the zone), COVERED (reload, laser cooldown, regen, face it),
  PEEK (step out to the nearest point that sees the target, shoot, duck back when hit / dry / fired / 2.2 s).
  Unseen shooters are placed 100 m out along the damage bearing. Being shot outranks the zone below 60 HP/s.

- Speed: A* stops at a 2.5 ms wall-clock deadline (one 2500-node step took ~15 ms); perch geometry
  precomputed (spot scoring 11 ms -> 1.8 ms); gc.freeze() after init. Replay max 7.8 ms.

@@@ kyoto-max__Mech_Royale 7723212 11-21 06:12
Phantom: hide in offline-computed low-exposure spots
Every survivor-family run scored 3.4-3.6 regardless of aim, firing or
weapons, so the score isn't decided by how we fight: we get found.
The map is identical every match, so visibility is precomputed:
- tools/exposure.py: for every standable 4 m cell, count viewers (8 m

@@@ niranjankumarnk__mech-royale d308a0c 11-20 21:45
Experiment F: free-for-all package and sturdier navigation on top of E
Practice fighting, looting and upgrade order are experiment E's. Roof
play (experiment R, 2.40) is switched off.

Free-for-all side:
- recognise a free-for-all within seconds: one death we did not cause in
  the first 30 s (two later), or two of three softer signs
- then stay out of sight of every known mech, run to the nearest cover
  by walking distance when seen, loot only where nobody is looking,
  fight only with a clear advantage or a pursuer that will not let go
- behave that careful way for the first 20 s of every match

Navigation:
- walkability checked metre by metre on the terrain grid
- jump and jet over what holds the mech up (pressed against something,
  or 3 s without progress): gets it out of the stadium bowl

Behaviour switches are now a runtime Policy; the simulator can run
policies against each other and replay recorded matches as ghosts.

@@@ niranjankumarnk__mech-royale 4ab8a70 11-20 21:05
Experiment R: fight from a roof against the practice squad
On top of experiment E. Against the practice squad only (off once a
free-for-all is detected):
- pick the nearest big flat roof (at least 9 m deep, 11 to 45 m up) that
  is well inside the next circle and has a clean wall to climb
- take a needed weapon lying within 90 m first, then go to the foot of
  the wall (shooting back on the way), jump and jet up, land 4 m inside
- on the roof: rest in the middle where the ground near the building
  cannot see us, step to 3 m from the edge to shoot down at a target,
  step back while the gun reloads or when hurt, look over an edge every
  10 s when nobody is in sight
- come down on the side of the next circle when the zone calls; drop
  off the far side if two hunters are up with us or one is and we are
  losing; a roof that fails twice is not tried again

Also: the path planner's memory is touched at start-up, and a search is
skipped (the current path kept) if a decision has already taken 12 ms.

Dev tools: the simulator now has jump, jet, gravity and roofs, and can
make hunters appear on the roof (SIM_CLIMB) to test being followed.

On top of experiment D, one change: the order in which upgrades are
picked. Versions up to D took armor, plating and nanites first. E takes

@@@ nshuai808__mech-royale c995b28 11-20 20:01
Add local logging harness: record, replay, analyze, botlog.trace
Matches show nothing but the score, so these stdlib-only tools give local
visibility into the bot:

- tools/record.py: transparent proxy around any bot command; logs every
  message, answer times, and botlog traces to replays/*.jsonl.gz
- tools/replay.py: feeds a recorded stream (default: the kit's 300 obs)
  to the bot lockstep, like the server; works inside the docker sandbox
- tools/analyze.py: report (timing, HP, zone, damage by weapon/attacker,
  rear hits, loot, modes, last seconds, timeline), CSV export, and --diff
  between two bot versions
- botlog.py: per-decision trace, off unless MECH_TRACE=1
- CLAUDE.md: game digest, tool usage, workflow, and status for new sessions

@@@ prakash-218__Buildathon-sessions a17ca33 11-20 23:41
Write each event once; bit filter for renamed IDs
- Events: a valid copy's 24-byte payload goes straight into its
  person's shard at parse time; every copy also sends a 24-byte
  (event_id, ingest_ts, payload location) record to its event_id
  shard. Dedup keeps the smallest ingest_ts per ID and marks the other
  copies' payloads dead in place, so the second reshard of all events
  (and the 40-byte intermediate records) is gone.
- A 2 MB bit filter of the renamed IDs lets most rows skip the
  ID -> name maps, which do not fit in cache.
- Canonical p<digits> product IDs are looked up in an array; any other
  form still goes through the exact map.
- Exit right after the outputs are written instead of freeing
  gigabytes of buffers.

36/36 fixtures on all three key types; exact matches on dev-answer and
on the reference for seeds 2, 3 and 11. Back to back with f1a698d on a
loaded laptop it ran about 25% faster in both pairs (timings noisy).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ prakash-218__Buildathon-sessions f1a698d 11-20 20:19
Parallel ID linking, mimalloc, buffer reuse
- Links: number the IDs in 256 hash shards in parallel and run the
  union-find over u32 indices; the ID -> name map is built as 256
  shard maps in parallel. 1.0-1.4 s -> about 0.3 s on 20M events.
- mimalloc as the global allocator, with MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=-1 so
  freed memory is reused: page faults per 20M run 497k -> 16k.
- Reuse each worker's dedup map and per-shard buffers across shards.
- Parquet without dictionaries or statistics: write 0.6 s -> 0.2 s.

Still 36/36 fixtures on all three key types, and exact matches on
dev-answer and on the reference for seeds 2, 3 and 11. The 20M run
takes 4.3-4.8 s locally (was 5.8-8.4 s).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ prakash-218__Buildathon-sessions 581d3f3 11-20 19:54
Speed up parsing and key handling
- Scan each chunk once with AVX2: 64 bytes at a time become newline,
  comma and quote bitmasks, replacing about 8 memchr calls per line.
- Pack IDs into order-preserving integers: u64 (up to 9 ASCII bytes,
  every generated ID), else u128 (up to 15 bytes), else redo the run
  with byte-slice keys. Hashing and comparing no longer read the input.
- Build for x86-64-v3 with fat LTO; ask the kernel to read the inputs
  ahead.
- docker_run.py: CPUSET to pin CPUs like the scorer, KEYS to force the
  fallback key types.

Passes 36/36 fixtures on all three key types, and matches dev-answer
and the reference on seeds 2, 3 and 11 exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ prakash-218__Buildathon-sessions a6ee49b 11-20 18:49
Add Rust pipeline and Dockerfile
A parallel Rust implementation of rules.md: mmap'd inputs cut into
line-aligned chunks, union-find for linked IDs, event dedup sharded by
event_id, then per-person sessions, click credit and assists (merged
7-day intervals per campaign). Writes one Parquet file per thread.

Passes all 36 fixtures, matches dev-answer exactly, and matches the
reference on seeds 2 and 3. A 20M-event run takes about 9.5 s locally
on 8 CPUs.

Also adds scripts/docker_run.py to run the image with the scorer's
container flags (works on Windows, and on Docker volumes).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ prakash-218__buildathon-blast 158c260 11-21 00:06
v3: trace import-time code to the bodies it serves; index dynamic imports
- dev/importtrace.py records, for each function run at import, the class or
  module body line that called it; a change there selects that body's users
  (narrowed by the assigned name / table entry) instead of every test
- index import_module(f"prefix.{...}") call sites so tests that load a
  module by computed name count as its users
- one-line def stubs are signature changes
- in-container test runs disabled (BLAST_NO_RUN=1): the in-process runner
  skips pickling across process pools and can miss serde failures

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@@ prakash-218__buildathon-blast fec4c8d 11-20 22:18
v2: per-test isolated coverage, source reads, safer refinements
- coverage re-recorded with each test in a fresh process (lazy caches such
  as the generator dispatch table now count for every test that needs them)
- record .py source reads and directory listings by tests
- always keep tests whose own code reads a changed table/attribute
- changed statements that run at import time select everything
- heavy-test statement refinement only for in-body modifications
- module-level changes follow importers transitively; new/deleted files
  select tests that scan their directory
- skip running when the total saving is below the preload cost
